findings.title: The ownership predicate excludes Java-valid curly-quoted inline commands
findings.java_mechanism: CommandFactoryNote.singleLine delimits DISPLAY with [%g]. Pattern2 expands %g to ASCII double quote, Unicode left/right double quotes, and the Jaws invisible quote marker. The exact Java revision therefore accepts the two preserved curly-quoted commands as named notes.
findings.rust_mechanism: parse_named_note_inline and looks_like_named_note_inline_command both hard-code ASCII double quotes. The valid Java opener is neither parsed nor claimed as an invalid owned command, so family parsing continues.
findings.downstream_mutation: The later relation materializes the missing code as an Interface in Component and as a root Default Deployment node with a new quark order. This is the exact accidental AST mutation the mechanism claims to prevent.

findings.title: Deployment does not retain the Java-valid note-on-link control
findings.java_mechanism: DescriptionDiagramFactory registers CommandFactoryNoteOnLink for the shared DESCRIPTION family, and its single-line grammar accepts 'note on link : bundle edge'. Java attaches the preserved text to the preceding Worker-to-Bundle link.
findings.rust_mechanism: Component has an explicit note-on-link branch, but Deployment has none. After named and attached note handling, an unmatched line reaches the end of the loop and parse_deployment still returns Ok.
findings.impact: The account claims valid note-on-link commands remain owned by a distinct factory, but the Deployment output silently omits the note. This also shows the all-lines-consumed Java model is not represented by the Rust family parser beyond the two newly guarded prefixes.

findings.title: Java provenance is incomplete and the plain-note control is not valid Java syntax
findings.detail: The account cites CommandFactoryNote but omits Pattern2, which defines the quote alphabet that defeats the implementation. It also says plain floating notes remain owned by a distinct factory, but DescriptionDiagramFactory registers named, attached, and link note factories only; both preserved 'note : ...' probes are Java syntax errors. The invalid probes do not count toward held-out coverage.

findings.title: The narrow invalid-suffix terminal guard works on the sampled failures
findings.detail: Invalid code punctuation, decoration reordering, unknown color, and composite color all reject before Rust emits an AST. No later endpoint or relation mutation occurs in those four probes.

anti_overfit_audit.unexplained_branch_or_grammar_issue: The two general prefix regexes are not fixture-shaped, but their ASCII-only quote grammar was derived without the Pattern2 %g dependency and is therefore incomplete.
anti_overfit_audit.evidence: The implementation diff adds only shared prefix predicates, terminal error branches, and bounded unit cases. No shipping-code check names this mechanism, a held-out label, a corpus path, golden bytes, coordinates, or branch counts.

residue_assessment: Exact Java/Rust error SVG artwork, error line choice, and diagnostic wording were not compared; rejection depends on Java-valid acceptance and AST semantics instead.
The Unicode-code SVG qualified-name normalization observed in the valid Component multiline control was not counted as a terminal-rejection failure.

The Deployment-shaped invalid plain-note source selecting Rust's Class parser falls under the account's declared top-level subtype residue; it is preserved only as evidence that the claimed plain-note Java control is not valid.
required_follow_up: Do not accept this mechanism. Model CommandFactoryNote's quote delimiters from Java Pattern2 %g in both the parser and ownership predicate, add valid curly-quoted Component and Deployment regressions with later relations, and either implement Deployment note-on-link ownership or narrow and correct the account's control claim with a separate convergence target. Remove or correct the assertion that plain floating 'note : ...' is valid in Java Description diagrams.
verdict_reason: REJECT. Six fresh Java-valid held-outs exercised family, inline/multiline form, decoration and color order, aliases, nesting, attached/link controls, and later relations. Three fail the claimed equivalence: two valid curly-quoted named notes fall through and permit later relations to synthesize ordinary endpoints, and one valid Deployment note-on-link is silently dropped. The sampled invalid named-note suffixes do terminate correctly, but that narrower success does not establish the claimed command-factory ownership model.
